summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 6, part 2) in which a first-person narrator fights his way through the Grigoryan estate. He disarms and kills goons with a borrowed M16, jams Goon #2's AK-style weapon, leaves the Grigoryan brother stunned, and then switches to semiauto to pick off guards at long range while clearing an exit. The passage stresses his skill and his detachment from the violence.
one_line: A first-person action excerpt in which the narrator fights goons at the Grigoryan estate with a borrowed M16 and clears a path out.
key_facts: The narrator wrenches an M16 away from a goon, and the momentum carries it toward Goons #1 and #2 stock first.
The narrator dives into a roll while Goon #2 is still turning, and Goon #1 fires a burst of automatic gunfire that sprays over the narrator's head.
The M16 had been set on full auto, and the narrator's burst makes Goon #1 fall backward through a glass bookcase.
Three goons are neutralized in about two and a half seconds.
The narrator tells Grigoryan that he jammed Goon #2's weapon, and says AKs are a lot sturdier than M16s.
Goon #2 pulls the trigger on his weapon and nothing happens.
The narrator says 'Bye now' to Grigoryan and leaves the room, keeping an eye on him the whole time.
Grigoryan's cigarette dangles forgotten from a corner of his mouth as the narrator leaves.
The narrator flicks the M16's selector lever to semiauto, reasoning that automatic fire is for people more concerned with looking impressive and chewing up furniture.
The narrator notes that an M16 can hit a target six hundred meters away with accuracy.
The narrator describes himself as 'a fucking computer program' when it comes to guns.
Grigoryan probably raised every alarm in the place before the narrator entered the room.
The narrator compares the sniping to 'a particularly artistic mathematical proof' in which each step follows from the last.
